subject: Arabic
source: Drive: Curriculum/Arabic folder and Secondary Lesson Plan - Arabic - Y8 (format and approach); Madinah-style progression (present tense verbs, question words); National Curriculum KS2 languages

lessons.title: What I do: verbs with I, he and she
objectives: Say five common verbs in the present tense
Change the verb for أَنَا، هُوَ، هِيَ
Make short sentences with verb and object
starter: Say 'I live in London' in Arabic.
Say 'she is a teacher' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Bismillah and action words
bullets: Today: I write, I read, I go
teach.note: Begin with bismillah. Mime actions (writing, reading) and elicit English verbs. Explain that Arabic verbs change their first letter depending on who does the action. Today we focus on I, he and she.

teach.heading: I do: the letter أ
teach.note: Point out the أ at the start for 'I'. Model with actions. Pupils echo and mime. Error: omitting the hamza. Emphasise that ana + verb starting with أ is common.

teach.heading: He does: the letter ي
teach.note: Replace أ with ي for 'he'. Use pictures of a boy doing each action. Pupils say: هُوَ يَكْتُبُ. Remind them that pronouns are optional but helpful.

teach.heading: She does: the letter ت
teach.note: Replace أ with ت for 'she'. Warning: ت is also used for 'you (boy)', so context matters. Show girl pictures. Practise with a quick-fire pronoun game.

teach.heading: Verb + object
teach.note: Add objects: the object takes -a (fatha) as in uhibbu sentences. Practise reading and translating. Pupils make new sentences with different verbs and objects.

practice: Say 'I do not like fish' in Arabic.
Choose the right verb form for each picture: أَكْتُبُ / يَكْتُبُ / تَكْتُبُ.
Create a sentence using a verb and an object.
independent: Write six sentences with different verbs and pronouns.
Fill in the gaps: ___ الْكِتَابَ (أَقْرَأُ / تَقْرَأُ / يَقْرَأُ)
Draw a picture of a person doing an action and write the sentence.
exit: How do you say 'she reads' in Arabic?
Which letter starts the verb for 'I'?
lessons.homework: Write sentences about what you, your father and your mother do each day.
lessons.send: SEND: verb cards with picture and mime, limit to three verbs. EAL: bilingual verb list. Stretch: add objects and adjectives to make longer sentences.

lessons.title: My daily routine
objectives: Describe five parts of a daily routine in Arabic
starter: Say 'I read the book' in Arabic.
What is the first letter of 'I' verbs?

teach.heading: In the morning
teach.note: Start with bismillah. Act out waking up, praying, eating breakfast. Pupils echo. Note: for Fajr we say 'I wake up for the Fajr prayer'. Sensitively allow pupils who do not pray yet to talk about others.

teach.heading: Going to school
teach.note: Introduce ilaa = to. Add أَتَعَلَّمُ (I learn). Pupils make a sentence about school. Highlight the repeated pattern verb + object.

teach.heading: Afternoon and evening
teach.note: Show a clock picture or sun/moon. Pupils say the time-of-day phrases: فِي الصَّبَاحِ، بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ، فِي الْمَسَاءِ، فِي اللَّيْلِ. Practise with mime.

teach.heading: Order with words
teach.note: Teach connecting words to sequence the routine. Model: أَوَّلًا أَسْتَيْقِظُ، ثُمَّ أُصَلِّي. Pupils build their own two-sentence routines. Display a model on screen.

teach.heading: Model paragraph
teach.note: Read the three-sentence paragraph aloud together. Ask comprehension questions in English. Encourage pupils to adapt for themselves; check verb forms.

practice: Make three sentences: I write, he reads, she goes.
Order the routine pictures and say each sentence.
Pair work: ask 'What do you do in the morning?' in English; answer in Arabic.
independent: Write a five-sentence routine using أَوَّلًا and ثُمَّ.
Match routine pictures to Arabic sentences.
Perform your routine for a partner.
exit: How do you say 'I go to school' in Arabic?
lessons.homework: Write your own morning routine in Arabic (4-5 sentences).
lessons.send: SEND: picture sequence cards and sentence frames. EAL: bilingual routine glossary. Stretch: add evening routine with salah and the connectives.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: My day and asking questions
lessons.title: Asking questions in Arabic
objectives: Use question words مَنْ، مَاذَا، أَيْنَ، مَتَى، كَيْفَ، لِمَاذَا
Use لِأَنَّ to give a reason
starter: Say 'I wake up in the morning' in Arabic.
Say 'I return to the house' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Question words
teach.note: Show a poster with the words. Pupils say each word with a gesture. Ask simple questions: مَنْ هَذَا؟ (who is this?) and مَاذَا تَقْرَأُ؟ (what do you read?). Clarify that مَاذَا is mostly used with verbs, while مَا is used in مَا هَذَا؟.

teach.heading: When, how and why
teach.note: Practise with questions: مَتَى تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ؟ كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ لِمَاذَا تَقْرَأُ؟ Pupils answer in simple Arabic. Note the pattern for 'you' (to a boy): ta- at the start.

teach.heading: Because
bullets: I read because reading is useful
teach.note: Explain that li'anna introduces a reason. Model with a simple sentence. Link to the Qur'an: the first command was 'Iqra' (read) in Surah al-Alaq 96:1.

teach.heading: Question and answer
teach.note: Present question + answer pairs. Pupils read them in pairs, then swap. Highlight that the answer repeats the verb. For a girl 'you', mention تَقْرَئِينَ as an extension.

teach.heading: Interview
teach.note: Pupils interview a partner with three questions from the poster, then report back. Teacher listens for correct question words. Provide model answers for support.

practice: Say 'I go to the mosque' in Arabic.
Match question words to English meanings.
Ask a partner مَتَى تَنَامُ؟ and answer.
independent: Write five questions with different question words.
exit: How do you say 'where do you go?' in Arabic?
lessons.homework: Write a mini-interview with five questions and answers.
lessons.send: SEND: question word cards and sentence frames. EAL: write English meaning beside each question. Stretch: write a dialogue of eight lines with reasons.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: My day and asking questions
lessons.title: Writing about my day
objectives: Plan a short paragraph in Arabic
Join sentences using وَ، ثُمَّ، بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ
starter: Say three question words in Arabic.
Ask 'when do you sleep?' in Arabic.
Say 'I read because it is useful' in Arabic.

teach.heading: Plan the paragraph
teach.note: Show a paragraph plan: opening, three actions, closing. Explain that good writing has order. Use a model: يَوْمِي: أَوَّلًا أَسْتَيْقِظُ ...

teach.heading: Model paragraph
teach.note: Read the paragraph twice. Ask pupils to underline verbs and connective words. Translate together. Identify first-person verbs beginning with أ.

teach.heading: Add detail
teach.note: Show how to expand sentences: add a person (مَعَ أَخِي), a place, a reason. Model expansions. Pupils add one detail to each sentence.

teach.heading: Check your writing
bullets: Do the verbs start with أ?
teach.note: Give a checklist. Pupils swap and peer-check. Common errors: missing hamza, wrong adjective ending, wrong direction when writing. Reinforce proofreading.

teach.heading: Write and share
teach.note: Allow 10 minutes to write. Pupils read aloud. Praise effort and accuracy. Collect writing for assessment of progress in Arabic script and grammar.

practice: Write the Arabic for 'I go to school'.
Underline the verbs in the model paragraph.
independent: Write a six-sentence paragraph about your day using أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ، أَخِيرًا.
Swap with a partner and check against the checklist.
Rewrite with corrections and add a reason with لِأَنَّ.
lessons.homework: Write a final copy of your paragraph neatly and bring a copy to share.
lessons.send: SEND: structured paragraph frame with gaps. EAL: bilingual checklist. Stretch: write a second paragraph about the weekend.
